lokasenna.excerpt: 3. “In shall I go | into Ægir’s hall, For the feast I fain would see; Bale and hatred | I bring to the gods, And their mead with venom I mix.” Eldir spake: 4. “If in thou goest | to Ægir’s hall, And fain the feast wouldst see, And with slander and spite | wouldst sprinkle the gods, Think well lest they wipe it on thee.” Loki spake: 5. “Bethink thee, Eldir, | if thou and I Shall strive with spiteful speech; Richer I grow | in ready words If thou speakest too much to me.” Then Loki went into the hall, but when they who were there saw who had entered, they were all silent. narrativeBlocks.title: Loki approaches the feast
narrativeBlocks.body: In Lokasenna, Loki arrives at Aegir's hall after a warning from Eldir. His stated purpose is to provoke the assembled gods, not to mediate their dispute.

narrativeBlocks.title: Speech becomes the action
narrativeBlocks.body: The poem stages a contest of insults and accusations. Its Loki is a literary speaker in this feast scene, not a complete summary of the figure across Norse texts.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep this poem's frame visible
narrativeBlocks.body: Lokasenna is an Eddic poem, translated and transmitted in a medieval manuscript. Read its hostile speech as a scene with a particular dramatic purpose.

narrativeBlocks.title: An uneasy guest
narrativeBlocks.body: The poem's tension comes from Loki's position inside the feast and his choice to attack its hosts in words.
